question.prompt: An error of \(0.02''\) is made in the measurement of a line \(10''\) long, while an error of only \(0.2''\) is made in a measurement of a line \(100''\) long. In comparison with the relative error of the first measurement, the relative error of the second measurement is:

solutions.explanation:
Relative error is the size of the measurement error divided by the actual length, with both expressed in the same units. The two relative errors are
\[
\frac{0.02}{10}=0.002,
\qquad
\frac{0.2}{100}=0.002.
\]
They are equal, so the answer is choice B.
solutions.title: Compare relative errors
